title: OneAquaHealth Protocol 1: Urban Stream Surface Foam & Surfactant Triage
content: Detergent surfactants and graywater discharges create distinctive white, billowing, cohesive foam along stream riffles, stormwater outlets, and eddy pools. Natural organic foam (decaying humic acids) is typically thin, brownish or tan-colored, and dissipates rapidly upon agitation. Thick white foam lasting >10 minutes with mild fragrance or sewage odor indicates direct greywater or industrial laundry effluent. Immediate field inspection is mandated when foam patches exceed 2 square meters near residential storm drains.

thresholds.low: Sparse natural brownish foam near natural organic debris / leaf litter
thresholds.moderate: Localized white foam patches (<1m2) near stormwater drain outlet
thresholds.high: Thick continuous white foam blanket (>2m2) accompanied by greywater clouding
thresholds.critical: Dense billowing foam bank (>5m) actively entering main river stem with noticeable chemical/perfumed scent

recommended_actions: Dispatch stormwater inspector to trace upstream storm sewer junction
Take grab sample for anionic surfactant (MBAS) testing
Log photo evidence with GPS coordinate verification
source_document: OneAquaHealth Framework WP3: Urban Aquatic Physical-Chemical Indicators Guideline, Sec 4.1

title: OneAquaHealth Indicator 2: Visual Assessment of Cyanobacteria & Eutrophic Algal Blooms
content: Urban runoff rich in fertilizer phosphates and nitrates induces severe cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) proliferation and green filamentous algal mats. Cyanobacteria blooms appear like spilled pea soup, bright green paint slicks, or blue-green scums on calm waters. Filamentous green algae form submerged hair-like strands or floating green carpets. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: Photographs can document the visual presence of green surface scum or turbidity, but cannot determine microcystin or cyanotoxin concentration without laboratory ELISA or spectrometry.
key_indicators: musty or septic decaying vegetation odor

thresholds.low: Scattered filamentous green algae clinging to rocks (<15% benthic cover)
thresholds.moderate: Green surface patches covering 15-40% of pond/stream surface
thresholds.high: Dense pea-soup cyanobacterial film covering >40% surface with visible surface scum
thresholds.critical: Complete blue-green scummy blanket with dead fish or severe anoxic septic odor

recommended_actions: Issue recreational water advisory prohibiting pet and human immersion
Perform microcystin cyanotoxin laboratory assay
Evaluate upstream nutrient loading from urban lawn fertilizers or sewage overflows
source_document: OneAquaHealth Biomonitoring Protocol: Harmful Algal Blooms in European Urban Catchments, Annex B

title: OneAquaHealth Metric 3: Solid Waste & Macroplastic Accumulation Index (SWAI)
content: Macroplastic waste (>5mm) such as single-use plastic bottles, polyethylene bags, food packaging, and synthetic polystyrene fragments obstruct urban culverts, degrade riparian benthic habitat, and leach plasticizers. Visual citizen surveys count items per 100-meter reach. SWAI categorizes debris density into Clean, Moderate Litter, Heavy Accumulation, and Severe Choke Points.

thresholds.low: Fewer than 5 visible macroplastic items per 50m stream bank
thresholds.moderate: 6 to 25 items per 50m reach, mostly isolated along waterline
thresholds.high: 26 to 100 items per 50m, debris entrapment on woody snags
thresholds.critical: Over 100 items forming hydraulic damming/choke at bridges or culvert grates

recommended_actions: Schedule municipal riparian cleanup team dispatch
Install floating debris boom at culvert inlet
Document plastic manufacturer branding for municipal extended producer responsibility audit
source_document: OneAquaHealth Citizen Science Manual: Macroplastic & Solid Waste Monitoring in Urban Watercourses

title: OneAquaHealth Protocol 4: Visual Water Turbidity & Suspended Solids Classification
content: Water clarity is an essential visual proxy for total suspended solids (TSS) and sedimentation. Observations must distinguish between natural storm sediment pulse (uniform light brown silt after torrential rain) versus acute point-source industrial/construction mud dumping. Visual categories: Crystal Clear (stream bed stones sharply visible >1m depth), Slightly Turbid (benthos visible <0.5m), Milky/Cloudy (unidentified chemical or limestone suspension), Opaque Muddy (brown silt zero visibility), and Black/Septic (severe deoxygenation and anaerobic sulfide production).

thresholds.low: Crystal clear to slightly turbid with bed substrate stones clearly visible
thresholds.moderate: Milky or slightly murky water with reduced visibility (10-30cm)
thresholds.high: Opaque muddy orange-brown silt from active upstream construction runoff without silt fencing
thresholds.critical: Pitch black septic stream with hydrogen sulfide odor and zero transparency

recommended_actions: Check upstream civil engineering/construction sites for sediment containment failures
Deploy turbidimeter for NTU measurement
Inspect municipal sewer mains for collapse or cross-connection
source_document: OneAquaHealth Field Manual: Rapid Physical Water Quality Screening, Section 2.3

title: OneAquaHealth Guideline 5: Illicit Discharge & Pipe Outfall Triage
content: Outfall pipes flowing during dry weather (>72 hours without precipitation) represent probable illicit connections from industrial, commercial, or sanitary sewage networks. Key visual markers include discolored discharge plumes, unnatural elevated temperature (visible steam in cool weather), petroleum sheen with rainbow iridescence, or thick grey sewage fungus (Sphaerotilus natans). LIMITATION: An image of a pipe cannot identify exact chemical constituents (e.g. heavy metals, VOCs); prompt chemical grab sampling is required.
key_indicators: sewage fungus growth at pipe lip

thresholds.low: Trickling clear groundwater seepage from weep holes in retaining wall
thresholds.moderate: Turbid discharge with faint odor under low flow conditions
thresholds.high: Discolored continuous outfall plume with oily rainbow sheen or soapy white discharge
thresholds.critical: Direct raw sewage or chemical solvent discharge with strong noxious stench

recommended_actions: Emergency notification to municipal illicit discharge detection and elimination (IDDE) unit
Collect grab samples for ammonia, surfactants, conductivity, and E. coli lab testing
Trace pipe network using municipal GIS drainage cadastre
source_document: OneAquaHealth Urban Catchment Surveillance: Illicit Discharge Detection Manual, Chapter 5

title: OneAquaHealth Protocol 6: Benthic Macroinvertebrate Habitat & Bank Integrity
content: Healthy urban streams feature heterogeneous physical structure: coarse gravel/cobble riffles, stable vegetated banks, submerged root systems, and overhead tree canopy shade. Channelization with vertical concrete walls and silt-choked gravel destroys macroinvertebrate refuge (mayflies, stoneflies, caddisflies), favoring pollution-tolerant chironomids and tubifex worms. Bank erosion releases excess sediment that smothers fish spawning gravels.
key_indicators: coarse gravel riffles vs concrete channel
bank collapse or vertical soil scars

thresholds.low: Intact vegetated riparian corridor with diverse cobble substrate and clear water
thresholds.moderate: Minor bank undercut (<0.5m) and isolated trampled vegetation
thresholds.high: Extensive bank slope collapse with active mud slumping into watercourse
thresholds.critical: Total habitat degradation: channel stripped to concrete flume with continuous siltation

recommended_actions: Recommend bioengineering bank stabilization (willow stakes, coir logs)
Conduct kick-net macroinvertebrate biotic index survey (BMWP / ASPT score)
Establish 15-meter riparian buffer planting zone
source_document: OneAquaHealth Ecosystem Assessment: Habitat Integrity & Benthic Biotic Health, Module 4

title: OneAquaHealth Protocol 7: Hydrocarbon Sheen vs Natural Biofilm Differentiation
content: Iridescent films on water surfaces are frequently misidentified by citizens. Hydrocarbon petroleum slicks (motor oil, gasoline, diesel) will quickly swirl, blend, and reform into swirling rainbow patterns when poked with a stick or disrupted. Natural biogenic iron/manganese bacterial biofilms or natural lipid sheens are brittle; when disturbed with a stick, they fracture and break into rigid geometric plates or angular tiles that do not reform smoothly. AI must clearly note this distinction and avoid diagnosing diesel fuel without confirming disruption behavior.
key_indicators: swirling fluid film vs brittle fractured plates
petroleum/gasoline odor vs marshy vegetable smell

thresholds.low: Brittle, fracturing biogenic iron bacteria sheen in slow wetland pool (natural process)
thresholds.moderate: Isolated rainbow oil drip from street bridge storm run-off (<0.5m2)
thresholds.high: Continuous swirling hydrocarbon rainbow slick originating from vehicle yard or gas station
thresholds.critical: Heavy thick black fuel oil slick coating bank vegetation and waterfowl

recommended_actions: Deploy absorbent oil booms across stream constriction point
Conduct VOC photoionization detector field screening
Report immediately to environmental protection hotline
source_document: OneAquaHealth Field Diagnostic Guide: Surface Film & Hydrocarbon Incident Identification

title: OneAquaHealth Guidelines 8: Photographic Limitations & Laboratory Validation Mandate
content: CORE SCIENTIFIC CONSTRAINT: Photographic observation is strictly limited to macroscopic, optical, and morphological evidence (foam, color, turbidity, macroinvertebrates, trash, bank collapse). AI systems ARE STRICTLY PROHIBITED from claiming precise laboratory-grade chemical metrics (e.g. pH value, nitrate mg/L, dissolved oxygen ppm, lead/cadmium/heavy metal concentration, or bacterial pathogen counts like E. coli or Enterococci) solely from citizen photographs. All high-severity and critical assessments MUST prompt certified laboratory grab sampling and human specialist validation.
key_indicators: strict separation of visible signals from invisible chemistry
mandatory grab sample protocol for chemical claims

thresholds.low: Visual signals sufficient for baseline monitoring
thresholds.moderate: Visual anomalies require physical site verification within 48 hours
thresholds.high: Mandatory human review + certified laboratory grab sample collection
thresholds.critical: Emergency human verification + immediate multidisciplinary hazard response

recommended_actions: Reject or redact unsupported laboratory chemical claims in AI recommendations
Schedule accredited laboratory chemical panel (pH, DO, BOD5, Ammonia, Heavy Metals)
Verify observer submission with ground-truth sensor stations
source_document: OneAquaHealth Framework WP1: Scientific Rigor & Citizen Science Data Quality Assurance Protocol
